correctness.rationale: The monotone-difference decomposition generates exactly 3q vertices. Explicit coordinate dot products give squared norm (q+2)/(8(q-1)) and all zero/nonzero distance gaps. A positive convex combination of q contact vertices equals the proposed center; its squared-distance variance identity forces every other center to have strictly greater enclosing radius. Exact rational verification reports 6286 checks and independent vertex enumeration for q=2,3,4. All-q proof is algebraic, not based on finite testing.

value.rationale: The smallest Euclidean enclosing ball is a canonical, natural geometric extremum for a Monge polytope already studied for volume, Ehrhart, inradius and mean width. The theorem gives an exact all-dimensional center and radius, strict clearance formulas for every vertex class, a six-to-q contact collapse, and a limiting radius/diameter ratio. This is structural information not supplied merely by knowing the 3q vertices; it supports geometric bounding and comparative roundness of normalized Monge matrix models.
